subject: function to transform parameters coming from a mcmc.list to a named list

messages.author: bc11fbb928eb77ff
messages.subject: function to transform parameters coming from a mcmc.list to a named list
parts:
Dear all,

I am wondering whether there is a function in nimble or maybe coda that would transform a set of parameters from part of a mcmc.list (one line of one component of the mcmc.list) to a  named list (e.g. to be acceptable by $setInits function). I have not found one so far but I am unsure it does not exist. If not I can provide a proposal of code that could be included in Nimble if you find it interesting. If so, better to use the existing code.

Thanks in advance,

Frédéric

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: function to transform parameters coming from a mcmc.list to a named list
parts:
Frédéric, nimble does provide the ability to take a current set of MCMC samples and reframe it into a list structure - I believe what you're looking for.

This method (as.list, specific for operating on nimble's modelValues data structures) cannot operate simultaneously on multiple chains of output (an mcmc.list object, a list of arrays of MCMC samples), but rather only on a single array of MCMC samples resulting from one chain.  So, you'd have to run a single chain at a time.  After executing a single chain, if your compiled MCMC object is called Cmcmc, then you would call:

my_list <- as.list(Cmcmc$mvSamples)

This will extract the current array of MCMC samples, from the most recently executed chain, and store them into a list-style structure (my_list).

Give this a go, and let me know if this is what you were looking for.

Cheers,
Daniel

messages.author: bc11fbb928eb77ff
messages.subject: Re: function to transform parameters coming from a mcmc.list to a named list
parts:
Thank you Daniel for your quick answer.

Yet I think this is not exactly what I what looking for: I tried it on a mcmc object - not a mcmc.list - as well as on the line of a mcmc.object. Yet it did not put together - i.e. in a same list component- the different components of a vector or a matrix but kepts them separate. cf. a copy below:

as.list(modIBP1b_FactD_MMcf7cr7b53o4_PMcf11b5_Priors_distYNorm3b_NimABalphadzetadbeta_experbias_experprec_chikpiktau_Inits_btadjust6_s3[[1]][1,])

$`meanplot[11]`
[1] 0.3706063

$`meanplot[12]`
[1] 0.5352893

$`meanplot[13]`
[1] -0.4031905

$`meanplot[14]`
[1] -0.6263602

I would have liked that all the meanplot components are merged into a single vector in a single component of the resulting list.

Cheers,

Frédéric
